guidance.procedure: Run separate relation gates for each target; do not transfer a clause or example across targets merely because they share this skill. For technical-only scope, require exclusivity: mixed technical, commercial, financial, personal, or business categories oppose “only technical,” while generic “information” or media language alone does not prove either breadth. For express identification, ask whether all covered information must be marked, identified, designated, or made known as confidential; “may be marked,” reasonable awareness, or marking only one medium is not an all-information requirement. For oral inclusion, require the definition or operative coverage to include oral or verbal disclosure, following any identification and later-confirmation conditions to completion. For agreement confidentiality, require coverage of the agreement, its existence, terms, discussions, or negotiations. Test independent development and third-party receipt as distinct exceptions; prior knowledge and public availability cannot substitute for either. After choosing the relation, make a second membership pass through definition lead-ins, grammatical continuations, and numbered exceptions. Include every independently responsive member, but exclude headings, examples of content, and adjacent duties that do not establish that target predicate.

Analyze each lifecycle target independently using actor, act, object, trigger, coverage, duration, and exception. For termination return, require a return-or-destroy duty triggered by termination, expiration, or an expressly equivalent ending event; a duty triggered only by request or an evaluation milestone does not borrow a termination trigger from elsewhere. For survival, require an express post-termination continuation, stated survival period, or rule that identified obligations remain binding; the agreement’s term, severability, remedies, or continuing liability for earlier breaches is not enough. For post-return possession, decide polarity from the complete rule: an archival, backup, legal, audit, or dispute-retention exception can support permitted possession, while a command covering all information and copies with no-retention language can oppose it. A limited return duty may leave possession unsettled. Do not reuse return text as survival or retention evidence unless it independently states that predicate. Collect all responsive provisions and every span needed to complete triggers, alternatives, coverage, and exceptions; omit headings and neighboring mechanics.

First select the exact tested act—reverse engineer, solicit, disclose, copy, or use—then compare actor, object, modality, recipient class, conditions, exceptions, and quantifiers. Evidence for one act is not evidence for another. Keep employee sharing separate from outside-third-party sharing: permission limited to employees with a need to know supports the employee target but does not support sharing with consultants, agents, advisers, contractors, or affiliates. If outside disclosure is prohibited while only employees are allowed, that can oppose the outside-third-party proposition. Expand a defined representative class only when the operative disclosure rule incorporates it, and retain every need-to-know, consent, or confidentiality condition. For copying, require an express permission or prohibition to copy or reproduce; markings on copies, ownership, or a reference to existing copies is insufficient. For solicitation and reverse engineering, require the named or materially equivalent prohibited act and follow split lists through completion. For limited use, collect every independent operative purpose restriction, excluding recitals and definitions that merely describe the purpose. After relation choice, cite all responsive acts and incorporated conditions, not merely the shortest proof.

Use two independent predicate gates. For compelled notice, first locate a legal, regulatory, judicial, subpoena, public-records, or comparable compelled-disclosure mechanism; then require an operative duty to notify, communicate with, or give the discloser an opportunity to object. A permission to disclose, a compelled-portion limit, or a section lead-in alone is not notice evidence. Scan separately for each mechanism and include every independently responsive notice rule, following any split sentence to completion. For no-license, require an express denial of a license, right, title, use right, proprietary interest, or intellectual-property right. Confidentiality, ownership, access, return, restricted use, or the absence of a grant cannot substitute for that denial. Include each independent denial and its grammatical completion, but exclude headings and adjacent provisions that merely describe ownership or permitted use.

Express identification requires a condition covering all protected information; a broad definition, optional marking, or marking limited to one medium is insufficient. For oral inclusion, follow any contemporaneous designation and later written-confirmation conditions to completion. Agreement confidentiality requires operative coverage of the agreement, its existence, terms, discussions, or negotiations. Keep independent development and third-party receipt distinct from prior knowledge and public availability. (a) to keep confidential and not disclose to any third party, except with the written permission of the Disclosing Party, any part, or the whole, of any Proprietary Information disclosed to it under this Agreement;
(d) to restrict access to the Proprietary Information disclosed to it under the terms of this Agreement to those of its employees and officers who need to know the same for the Purpose.

“Affiliate” shall mean any corporation, partnership, or other entity that, either directly or indirectly, controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with a party, where control is defined as having more than a fifty percent (50%) controlling interest.
